# Signed Euler charges and an exact planar facet monotonicity

Registry audit: Sections 3–4 are an explicit Euler-coordinate calibration,
not a new geometric inequality. Their mechanisms already occur in
`candidate 8e69e6820cd6ee00`
and `candidate 929f9f6bc9acea34`.
The strict floating-body example in Section 2 and the exact aggregate
counterexample in Section 5 clarify the scope of a valuation approach.

The unrestricted OC conclusion is not proved here. The main positive result
is an exact local monotonicity for a sharp ordinary triangle cap circuit,
expressed as a signed boundary valuation. It identifies a concrete geometric
bridge for a mixed critical certificate: nonnegative Green potentials of the
actual boundary charges, with the correct affine cancellations. Pointwise
nonnegative Euler weights are impossible even for strict lattice-free
certificates containing a nonempty floating body and having equal cap masses.

The separate six-fiber construction below disproves a tempting stronger
aggregate inequality when its floating-body-origin hypothesis is omitted.
That construction must not be advertised as an obstruction to an actual
below-OC equal-critical menu.

## 1. Exact signed overlap identity

Let H_(s,j) be a finite cap family, grouped into projected-facet circuits,
and put U_s = union_j H_(s,j). All intersections below are restricted to
an actual source S and measured with its mixed measure mu. Suppose the
U_s cover S. Set b_s = max_j mu(H_(s,j)) and gamma = (d/(d+1))^d.
Then

    B = sum_s b_s - gamma M
      = sum_s [b_s - gamma mu(U_s)]
        + gamma [sum_s mu(U_s) - mu(union_s U_s)].                (1)

The last bracket is the integral of m(p)-1, where m is the number of
circuit unions containing p. It is nonnegative, but the first brackets
need not be. Equivalently its full Euler/Mobius expansion is

    B = sum_s b_s
        - gamma sum_(nonempty A subset [r])
                     (-1)^(|A|+1) mu(intersection_(s in A) U_s). (2)

On any parameter neighborhood with fixed maximizing indices j_s, B is
an actual signed valuation, with density

    w(p) = sum_s 1_(H_(s,j_s))(p) - gamma 1_(union_s U_s)(p).     (3)

One can instead average caps within each group with nonnegative weights
pi_(s,j) summing to one. This gives a smaller functional B_pi <= B.
Under equal cap masses the two agree. This is the relevant way of retaining
an equal critical budget while permitting a signed boundary charge.

Formula (1) keeps all cross-group overlaps. It is not a claimed inequality.

## 2. Equal caps and a nonempty floating body do not give pointwise weights

Take n=1, d=2, T a triangle of area V, and C=[0,1] x T. Its mixed
source consists of two equal triangle fibers. Write lambda_0,lambda_1,
lambda_2 for the affine barycentric coordinates of T and g for its centroid.
For i=0,1,2 define six CLOSED caps

    H_(0,i) = {lambda_i(x) - 3/10 - z >= 0},
    H_(1,i) = {lambda_i(x) - 3/10 - (1-z) >= 0}.                (4)

At its own integer fiber each cap has area (7/10)^2 V=49V/100.
At the other integer fiber it is empty, since its threshold is 13/10.
Thus all six cap masses are exactly equal. Both groups cover their own
entire triangle, since max_i lambda_i >= 1/3 > 3/10.

The complementary auxiliary polytope Q is bounded and full dimensional.
Its exact base projection is

    [1/30,29/30].                                                (5)

Indeed summing a group's three inequalities gives its indicated base
bound, and x=g satisfies all six inequalities throughout (5). At
(1/30,g), respectively (29/30,g), exactly the three inequalities of
that group are active; the other three have strict margin -14/15.
The two projected facets are indispensable for integer exclusion.

Let the raw floating-body threshold be alpha=99V/200. Every cap in (4)
has mass strictly below alpha, so the actual alpha-floating body is
contained in Q. It is NONEMPTY: the ordinary centerpoint theorem in
ambient R^3 gives a real point of depth at least M/4=V/2>alpha.
It contains no mixed-integer point, since every point of either extreme
triangle fiber can be isolated from the other fiber by a base tilt and
has ordinary triangle depth at most (4/9)V<alpha. Thus this is an actual
strict lattice-free floating-body certificate, not an empty-real-core
example. Its six specified caps have equal budgets. No assertion is
made that all six are supporting cuts of the exact floating body.

Nevertheless no probability weights pi_(s,0),pi_(s,1),pi_(s,2) can make

    sum_(s,i) pi_(s,i) 1_(H_(s,i)) - (4/9)1_S >= 0              (6)

pointwise. Near each vertex of each fiber there is an open set belonging
to exactly its one vertex cap. Therefore (6) would require each of the
three weights in each group to be at least 4/9, whereas their sum is one.
Higher intersection terms vanish on these singleton-membership regions.
The contradiction is 3*(4/9)>1.

The construction works with any t in (1-1/sqrt(2),1/3) in place of 3/10,
with own cap mass (1-t)^2 V, projection [1/3-t,2/3+t], and a threshold
strictly between that cap mass and V/2. As t increases to 1/3, it approaches
the actual sharp critical triangle circuits at the two integer centers.
Consequently pointwise positivity cannot be repaired merely by proximity
to the sharp equal-critical case. Integrated convexity must do real work.

## 3. Positive theorem: exact signed first variation at a sharp triangle

Fix the three sharp triangle caps H_i={lambda_i>=1/3}. For a nearby planar
convex body K define the equal-weight signed valuation

    E(K) = (1/3) sum_(i=0)^2 |K intersect H_i| - (4/9)|K|.       (7)

At K=T all three caps have mass (4/9)V, so E(T)=0. On any one edge of T,
parametrize by t in [0,1], with the two nonzero barycentrics t,1-t.
The boundary density of (7) is exactly

    w(t) = -1/9,      0<t<1/3 or 2/3<t<1;
            2/9,      1/3<t<2/3.                               (8)

In particular

    integral_0^1 w(t) dt = integral_0^1 t w(t) dt = 0.          (9)

For EVERY concave normal velocity v on this edge,

    integral_0^1 w(t)v(t) dt >= 0.                             (10)

Here the sign is outward normal speed. Formula (10) is an exact
first-variation fact for actual convex facet bulges; it is not a
pointwise assertion about w.

### Proof with all constants

Let

    G(s,t) = min{(1-t)s, t(1-s)}.

This is the Green tent with zero endpoint values and distributional
second derivative in s equal to -delta_t. A concave v with finite
endpoint slopes has the exact representation

    v(s) = (1-s)v(0) + s v(1) + integral_(0,1) G(s,t) d kappa(t),
    kappa = -v'' >= 0.                                         (11)

The affine contribution vanishes by (9). Direct integration gives

    K(t) := integral_0^1 w(s)G(s,t) ds

          = t^2/18,                        0<=t<=1/3;
            [6t(1-t)-1]/54,                1/3<=t<=2/3;
            (1-t)^2/18,                    2/3<=t<=1.          (12)

All three expressions are nonnegative, and K(t)>0 for 0<t<1.
Thus

    integral w v = integral K(t) d kappa(t) >= 0.              (13)

Approximation by concave piecewise affine functions gives the same
conclusion for every continuous concave v. Equality holds exactly for
affine v. This follows from strict positivity of K on the open interval.

For an edge of Euclidean length L, the physical contribution is L times
(13). A bounded Lipschitz concave outward bulge vanishing at the edge
endpoints is realized by replacing that edge by its outward graph at
height epsilon*v; for sufficiently small epsilon the enclosed body is
convex. The standard strip first-variation formula gives

    d/d epsilon E(K_epsilon)|_(0+) = L integral w v >= 0.       (14)

Intersections of moving strips with the fixed cap boundaries contribute
only O(epsilon^2). For simultaneous edge bulges, sum (14) over the three
edges. Endpoint motions contribute affine edge speeds and vanish to
first order by (9), whenever the indicated polyhedral first variation
exists.

This also gives an ACTUAL mixed convex deformation: use
C_epsilon=[0,1] x K_epsilon, retain the two isolated sharp cap circuits,
and apply the same deformation to both fibers. Its signed mixed
first variation is twice (14). The product's sharp cap budgets are equal.

There is no uniform positive multiple of total curvature in (13):
K(t) vanishes quadratically near either endpoint. Concentrating curvature
near vertices can make the response arbitrarily small.

## 4. Exact planar criterion for a general signed boundary charge

Let rho be any finite signed measure on a facet interval. Suppose it
annihilates affine functions:

    integral d rho = integral s d rho(s) = 0.                   (15)

Then the following conditions are equivalent:

(a) integral v d rho >=0 for every continuous concave v;
(b) K_rho(t):=integral G(s,t) d rho(s) >=0 for every t in [0,1]. (16)

Necessity uses the concave tests v=G(.,t); sufficiency is (11) and
approximation. For piecewise constant Euler densities this is an exact
finite calculation: K_rho is piecewise quadratic, satisfies
K_rho''=-rho in the distributional sense, and has zero endpoint values.
One need only inspect the breakpoints and the interior stationary points
of each quadratic piece.

Thus an aggregate Euler valuation need NOT have nonnegative pointwise
weights. Its correct local monotonicity test is positivity of these
Green potentials after the affine moments have been accounted for.
The ordinary sharp triangle passes the test with (12).

For a mixed critical certificate, the unproved bridge is to obtain this
positivity from the ACTUAL cap restrictions and actual feasible coupled
fiber deformations. A source facet generally sees oblique cap thresholds
that are not its own centroid thresholds; the calculation (12) cannot
simply be transplanted. Affine moments may cancel only after summing
across fibers, and feasible edge speeds may be coupled by convexity of
the whole source. Requiring every individual facet potential to be
nonnegative could therefore be stronger than necessary and is NOT proved.
A successful global argument would also still need an attained bad
extremizer and either strict improvement or a valid neutral-complexity
reduction. Nonnegative first variation alone is not an OC proof.

## 5. Exact warning: full cross-group Euler cancellation can still fail

This example falsifies the unconditional inequality

    sum_s max_j mu(H_(s,j)) >= (4/9)M.                          (17)

It has a genuinely minimal four-facet lattice-free certificate and strict
common contacts. It does NOT retain a nonempty floating body at its cap
budget, and has highly unequal group budgets. It is included to distinguish
what the exact identities prove from the additional critical hypotheses.

Let the lattice-complete projection have inequalities

    z1>=0, z2>=0, |z1-z2|<=1, z1+z2<=3.

Its integer points, in the order used below, are

    (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1),(2,1),(1,2).                        (18)

At the first three put centered squares of radius r=1/1000 and at the
last three put centered squares of radius R=1/100. Take their lifted
convex hull C. These are its exact integer fibers: five indices are
projection vertices; the remaining index (1,1) has its prescribed
maximal square and cannot be enlarged because every generating square
is contained in that square. C is a full-dimensional convex body.
Write v=4r^2 and V=4R^2=100v; then M=3V+3v=303v.

Use u1=(1,0), u2=(0,1), u3=(-1,-1), and

    ell_0=1/10-z1-z2,
    ell_1=z1-2z2-9/10,
    ell_2=-2z1+z2-9/10,
    ell_3=z1+z2-19/10.

Each affine q_s has two rows below; all displayed entries are divided
by 100 and each row acts on (z1,z2,1):

    q_0: (236,236,-520), (-267,31,260)
    q_1: (225,197,-565), (-192,139,203)
    q_2: (197,225,-565), (-336,-33,363)
    q_3: (271,271,-656), (-371,100,328).

Define H_(s,j)={u_j dot (x-q_s(z))+ell_s(z)>=0}.
The three continuous normals have positive multipliers 1/3 and rank two.
The complementary polytope Q satisfies all twelve reversed inequalities.
Its projection is contained in the bounded integer-free quadrilateral
L={ell_s<=0 for all s}. Integer exclusion is exact: an integer point of
L must have z1+z2=1; writing z1=k yields k<=0 from the second inequality
and k>=1 from the third. Each of the four inequalities is indispensable:
its own binary lattice point satisfies all three other inequalities.

Set

    r_0=(1/20,1/20),  r_1=(19/20,1/40),
    r_2=(1/40,19/20), r_3=(19/20,19/20).

At (r_s,q_s(r_s)), its own three inequalities are equalities and all
nine others have strictly negative margin, at most -923/2000. Hence all
four are genuine projected facets of Q, not invented Farkas directions.
Locally x=q_s(z) remains feasible on the appropriate side of that facet.
A convex average of the four contacts makes all twelve inequalities
strict, so Q is full dimensional. Boundedness follows from bounded L
and the positive spanning of the continuous normals.

Exact fiber clipping gives the cap masses, in units v:

    group 0: (3,0,0)
    group 1: (3,0,0)
    group 2: (3,0,1/2)
    group 3: (103,100,100).                                   (19)

The first three circuit unions are exactly the three small fibers;
the fourth circuit union is all of S. Thus the cross-group overlap
correction in (1) is (4/9)*9v=4v, and even after retaining it completely,

    B = 112v - (4/9)*303v = -(68/3)v <0.                       (20)

The fixed maximizing cap is j=1 in every group. Its signed density
(3) is 32/9 on the three small fibers, 5/9 on the large fiber (1,1),
and -4/9 on each of the other two large fibers. This independently
recovers (20).

There is also an exact convex deformation test: keep R=1/100 fixed
and vary 0<r<R/2 while retaining the fixed caps. All memberships in
(19) stay fixed, except for the already exact half-square trace.
Thus

    B(r) = -V/3 + (32/3)v = (128r^2-4R^2)/3,
    B'(r) = (256/3)r >0.                                     (21)

The sign changes at r=R/sqrt(32), without any change in the cap nerve.
Euler topology alone does not determine the sign.

Finally the missing floating-body hypothesis is explicit. At a common
strict budget alpha=104v every listed cap is bad. Any alpha-floating
body would lie in Q, hence in {z1+z2<=19/10}; that base halfspace has
only the three small fibers and mass 3v<alpha. Therefore the floating
body is empty. This example cannot be used against the equal-critical,
nonempty-floating-body bridge. It shows exactly why those hypotheses
cannot be dropped.

The companion exact verifier is
